title: September export boom is broad but marginal growth is semiconductor-concentrated
confirmed: Korea September exports were $120.94B, +83.5% y/y; imports $71.09B; trade surplus $49.85B.
Semiconductor exports were $60.3B, +262.8% y/y; daily average exports were $5.63B, +105% y/y.
Non-semiconductor exports were reported +23% y/y, so the boom is not exclusively semiconductors.
Using the published totals, semiconductors were about 49.86% of September exports.
Using published y/y rates, semiconductor export growth accounts for about 79.4% of the dollar increase in total exports; this is an AI-A derived arithmetic estimate, not an official statistic.
The ministry-attributed explanation says semiconductor export volume expanded while fixed prices also rose; exact HBM/DRAM/NAND price-volume decomposition is not yet available in the checked release.
hypothesis: Korea's export and trade-surplus beta is becoming more convex to the memory/AI cycle: ex-semiconductor exports are still growing, but roughly four-fifths of September's incremental export dollars can be attributed arithmetically to semiconductors. If memory ASP or AI CAPEX turns, macro export momentum and semiconductor-heavy equity earnings/foreign-flow expectations could weaken together; while the cycle persists, the same concentration amplifies upside.
unknown: How much of the semiconductor increase is timing/base effect versus durable run-rate
Whether foreign equity flows price this concentration before official trade data
Company-level Samsung Electronics versus SK hynix revenue read-through
counter_scenarios: Ex-semiconductor exports growing about 23% means underlying trade breadth is materially positive and can cushion a memory slowdown.
Higher-value product mix can sustain export dollars even if unit volumes flatten.
Semiconductor concentration can represent comparative advantage rather than fragility while AI investment and memory pricing remain strong.

derived_metrics.methodology: 603/1209.4; prior-year totals reconstructed as current/(1+yoy rate), then semiconductor dollar increase divided by total dollar increase. Rounded.

coverage_finding: At preflight, the 09:18 KST issue digest did not yet surface the 09:00 September export release as a top issue; fresh external discovery found the official-data report. Treat as a freshness/coverage candidate for AI-D/AI-E, not proof of collector failure until a later collector cycle is checked.

handoff.task: Backtest export-concentration shock: semiconductor share/contribution surprise -> Samsung/SK hynix relative returns, foreign spot/futures flows, USD/KRW, controlling for UST 10Y/30Y.
Falsify concentration-risk interpretation using ex-semiconductor breadth, base effects, ASP/product-mix effects and prior high-concentration export episodes.
Check whether the 09:00 MOTIE export release enters a later collector cycle as an independent event-core; if not, inspect official macro-release freshness/coverage.
